newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares weather profit-taking, end higher.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares weather profit-taking, end higher.

text.p: The Cairo stock exchange withstood another day of profit-taking on Tuesday and even rose in spite of slippages in the popular milling sector, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index gained 0.82 points to 276.87. The index slipped on Monday for the first time since it broke record highs last week.
"The market is relaxing slightly and investors are consolidating their gains as expected," said Youssef Khalil of brokerage house Delta-EAB.
Profit-taking infiltrated the milling sector, sending Central and West Delta Flour Mills shares falling 4.40 pounds to 83.60 and East Delta Flour Mills down 1.70 to 50.30.
Central Egypt Flour Mills shed 2.24 to 42.7 while Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 2.05 down at 71.00.
"The share prices shot up in (last week's) rise and now the prices are encouraging to sell," said Khalil.
Blue-chip cement firms helped keep the market solid and buoyed the day's 56.77 million pound ($16.70 million) turnover.
Helwan Portland Cement, the day's most active share, was also its biggest gainer and ended 6.50 pounds higher at 64.00.
The state earlier this week sold its majority in the firm to private investors.
Privatised Amriyah Cement gained 1.00 to 66.00 and Suez Cement rose 0.05 to 56.50.
Of a total 65 stocks traded, 20 rose, 13 fell and the rest closed unchanged.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 433.24 points from Monday's 432.8 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 190.17 from 189.37 points.
